task.title: Backing up Red Hat Quay on standalone deployments
task.shortdesc: To back up a standalone Red Hat Quay deployment, you can archive configuration files, dump the PostgreSQL database, and sync object storage blobs.

step.cmd: Create a temporary backup directory, for example, quay-backup:
The following example command denotes the local directory that the Red Hat Quay was started in, for example, /opt/quay-install:

info.p: Change into the directory that bind-mounts to /conf/stack inside of the container, for example, /opt/quay-install, by running the following command:

step.cmd: Compress the contents of your Red Hat Quay deployment into an archive in the quay-backup directory by entering the following command:

info.codeblock: config.yaml config.yaml.bak extra_ca_certs/ extra_ca_certs/ca.crt ssl.cert ssl.key

step.cmd: Back up the Quay container service by entering the following command:

info.codeblock:
$ podman inspect quay-app | jq -r '.[0].Config.CreateCommand | .[]' | paste -s -d ' ' -
/usr/bin/podman run --name quay-app \ -v /opt/quay-install/config:/conf/stack:Z \ -v /opt/quay-install/storage:/datastorage:Z \ registry.redhat.io/quay/quay-rhel9:v3.18.0
